audit.whatIsWrong: Six of the seven chart rows give the stage to Ziggs or call it even, while the whys attached to those same rows say the opposite in plain language: 'you stick him and land guaranteed true damage', 'he has no dash to escape', 'short axe-reset trades out-damage his poke', 'you ignore his entire zone and all-in him uncontested', 'he cannot open the distance his artillery poke depends on'. The page also grades the lane 8.5/10 difficulty and calls it a hard matchup on a 54.97% win rate.
audit.why: This is the worst chart-versus-prose split in the slice: the reader is told to survive a lane the same page says he dominates from Level 2 to first item. Only Level 1 is genuinely Ziggs's, and the two-item row is the one that neutralises Olaf.
audit.corrected: Skill at Level 1, Olaf from Level 2 through first item, Skill at two-plus items — matching the packet chart and every why on the page. Difficulty regraded to 6/10.

audit.whatIsWrong: Olaf's W is called omnivamp that heals minefield chip (Riot: attack speed and a shield). No ability is ever named or numbered — the packet reports zero sequencing cues. And early claims 'his bomb cooldown is too long to trade back' when Bouncing Bomb is 6s at rank 1 and 4s maxed.
audit.why: The real punish window is not his Q at all — it is Satchel Charge, 20/18/16/14/12s, which is both his knockback and his only escape. Pointing the player at the wrong cooldown is why the page has no sequencing advice that works.
audit.corrected: Bait Satchel Charge (20s at rank 1); Bouncing Bomb is only 6s so it is not the window; Hexplosive Minefield is a flat 16s; W shields, the passive life-steals.

audit.why: Spike shape is sound — Olaf at 2-3 and 6, Ziggs at Level 1 and again once artillery scales. spikes[3] correctly uses the Level 1-2 window rather than inventing a late one.
54.97% over 584 games — Olaf-favoured, which is why the difficulty grade and the chart both needed to move.

edits.before: Level 1 you have no answer to his long-range Q bomb yet, so he chips you walking up while you only farm — genuinely his window.
edits.after: Level 1 you have no answer to Bouncing Bomb at 850 range, so he chips you as you walk up to farm — genuinely his window.

edits.before: Your W-omnivamp heals the minefield chip while short axe-reset trades out-damage his poke through levels 4-5.
edits.after: W's shield eats the Hexplosive Minefield chip while short axe-reset trades out-damage his poke at 4-5.

edits.before: Ragnarok cleanses his W knockback and E minefield slow, so you walk through his entire zone and all-in uninterrupted.
edits.after: Ragnarok answers his Satchel knockback and the minefield slow — bait that 20s Satchel and he has no exit left.

edits.before: Level 1 is the only awkward part: Ziggs just chucks his long-range Q bomb at you while you walk up to farm, and you have no tool to answer poke yet, so take CS at max range and don't flame the chip damage. The lane flips at 2-3 — once you have Undertow plus Reckless Swing, you land a Q to slow him, pick the axe up for the cooldown refund, and chain a second slow into your E true-damage nuke. He cannot kite that, and his bomb cooldown is too long to trade back.
edits.after: Level 1 is the only awkward part: Ziggs chucks Bouncing Bomb at you from 850 while you walk up to farm, and you have no tool to answer poke yet, so take CS at max range and eat the chip. The lane flips at 2-3 — with Undertow plus Reckless Swing you land the axe, pick it up for the 9s refund, and chain a second slow into true damage. His only exit is Satchel Charge, 20s at rank 1, and once he spends it he is stuck with you.

edits.before: This is your takeover. Every time he steps up to poke or push, you Q-slow, walk on top of him with axe resets, and W-omnivamp heals back any minefield chip while E carves a guaranteed chunk out of his squishy frame. At 6 Ragnarok is the answer to his whole kit — it cleanses the W knockback and the E slow, so you charge straight through his zone and all-in. With Black Cleaver and your perma-slow online, he physically cannot make the gap his poke needs to survive.
edits.after: This is your takeover. Every time he steps up to poke or push, you Undertow him, walk on top with axe resets, and W's shield eats the minefield chip while Reckless Swing carves a chunk out of his squishy frame. At 6 Ragnarok is the answer to his whole kit — it takes the Satchel knockback and the minefield slow, so you charge straight through the zone and all-in. With Black Cleaver and perma-slow online, he cannot make the gap his poke needs.

edits.before: Drop E minefield and W on chokes to slow your engage and reset the gap after you ult
edits.after: Drop Hexplosive Minefield on chokes and Satchel to reset the gap after you ult

edits.before: His knockback + self-peel escape. Engage when it's down. Only engage once it is down or baited.
edits.after: Satchel Charge is 20s at rank 1 and knocks you both away — it is his only escape, so bait it first.

edits.before: - Ziggs Satchel Charge: matchup-defining — His knockback + self-peel escape. Engage when it's down. Track it before every engage. - Your committal tool: never spend it on chip. - Your ultimate: the win condition — kill windows only.
edits.after: - Satchel Charge: matchup-defining — 20s at rank 1, knocks you both away, and it is his only escape. Bait it, then commit. - Bouncing Bomb: 6s at rank 1, so it is chip, not a window. - Hexplosive Minefield: flat 16s slow.

edits.after: Overall difficulty: 6/10. The lane is decided by how well you bait Satchel Charge and how disciplined your pattern is.
